person.summary: I build AI systems that do the slow work and stop for a human yes: RAG assistants, career pipelines, research desks and on-device tools on .NET/C#, React and Python. Open them and test them here.

patterns.title: Sort incoming enquiries and draft the replies
steps: Connect the inbox you already use (email first; WhatsApp Business where its API allows).
Each new message is sorted: new {customer} enquiry, booking, complaint, spam.
A reply is drafted for each one and waits for you to read, edit and send.
Anything unanswered after a day shows up on a short reminder list.
patterns.guard: Nothing is sent without you pressing send.

proofs.quote: Added inbox watching so replies can be noticed, with notify paths that still require a person to send.
It labels each reply as interview, rejection or acknowledgement and shows the cues it used.

patterns.title: Answer {customer} questions from your own information, day and night
steps: Collect what you already tell {customers}: services, hours, prices you publish, policies.
The assistant finds the matching passage first, then answers from it and names its source.
Questions it cannot answer from your information are handed to you, not guessed.
patterns.guard: If the live AI is down, the page says so instead of pretending. Your API keys stay on the server.

proofs.quote: The question is matched locally, the passage is named, then Gemini answers.
If the live robot is unhealthy, the UI says it is demo coaching instead of pretending.
Key location. VPS only. Same-origin proxy. Not shipped to the browser.

patterns.title: Draft quotes, proposals and letters from your real details
steps: Keep one source of truth: your services, standard wording and the facts of each job.
Paste the request; a first draft is written using only those facts.
You review, change and send it yourself.
patterns.guard: Drafts only, never invented details, never sent automatically.

proofs.quote: AI Hawk writes a cover note and CV synopsis for one role, built only from facts on the published CV and case studies, with sources.
Not autonomous: no auto-apply, no auto-send, no irreversible decision.

patterns.title: A daily watch with a short morning report
steps: Pick the public sources worth watching (supplier prices, tenders, listings, reviews).
A scheduled job collects them read-only and ranks what changed.
You get one short report with links, at a time you choose.
patterns.guard: Read-only collection from public pages; it never logs in or buys on your behalf.

proofs.quote: Daily scrape at 20:00 SAST across public listings. Read-only collection.
Published numbers only: ~60s quote refresh, 24 sessions / 2h idle, ~87 MB desk, backoff on 429 and 5xx.

patterns.title: Match each request to the right service, product or person
steps: Describe your services, products or team members in plain language.
Each incoming request is ranked against them by meaning, not just keywords.
You see the top match with the reason, and decide.
patterns.guard: Rankings are suggestions with a reason attached, never automatic decisions.

proofs.quote: A hashed sentence embedding ranks each posting against JobNet, Assist, THINK, Forex, and SoundX, and keeps one role per company.
Sentence embeddings (MiniLM, self-hosted, in a background worker) compare each requirement with real CV evidence

patterns.title: Read slips, invoices and forms into a spreadsheet
steps: Snap or upload the slip, invoice or form.
Text is read on the device and the fields (date, items, total) are pulled out.
You check the totals before anything is saved to your sheet or accounting tool.
patterns.guard: The image stays on the device for reading; totals are checked, not trusted blindly.

proofs.quote: Hum detection, OCR, and the agent visualiser.

patterns.title: Understand your numbers with honest dashboards
steps: Bring the sales or bookings data you already keep.
A dashboard shows trends, and a simple model is tested against a plain baseline.
If the model is no better than the baseline, the dashboard says so.
patterns.guard: Every chart shows its data source and date; weak models are labelled, not hidden.

proofs.quote: Useful provenance on a response: timestamp, data source, and whether the line is observation, analysis, or simulation.
Sentence embeddings (MiniLM, self-hosted, in a background worker) compare each requirement with real CV evidence

patterns.title: Bookings, shifts and check-ins with sign-off steps
steps: Map the flow you run today: booking, reminder, check-in, payment, dispute.
Each step gets a clear status and an approval point where money or people are involved.
An assistant explains the rules to staff and {customers}, without making up amounts.
patterns.guard: Money, payouts and personal data always pass a human sign-off. POPIA consent is designed in.

proofs.quote: Event-flow screens and architecture diagrams: signup, rate lock, check-in, payout, disputes, compliance gates. Reference drawings, not a live service.
When it doesn't know, it says so.

patterns.title: A voice assistant for hands-busy work
steps: Decide the few jobs worth doing by voice: look up a price, log a job, read a message.
Speech goes to an assistant that answers or drafts, through your own server.
Anything that changes records is confirmed on screen first.
patterns.guard: Per-user caps and a server-side key; actions are confirmed before they happen.

proofs.quote: Built THINK as a React 19, Vite, and TypeScript workspace: chat, image, live voice over WebSocket, plus sites, code, and a learning path.
